## Trial `traffic-shaping-rhel10__yk54Rsg`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All three material outcomes of the task were directly and coherently demonstrated: the previously-unconfigured private links were established so node2/node3 route through node1, a VyOS htb qos shaper was applied to the node3-facing egress link limiting node2->node3 to ~0.84-0.92 Mbit/s (down from a ~20 Gbps baseline), and node3->node2 remained unrestricted (~1.5 Gbps) throughout. The executor additionally ran the provider-wide restart evidence protocol on all three nodes with clear pre-restart boot-identity/healthy-state capture, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state (including a re-verified 1 Mbit/s cap after all three nodes were rebooted), well beyond what the public task contract required, and cross-checked cleanly against the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. Minor hygiene residue (uncleaned test-result JSON and log files in /tmp on node2/node3) is the only notable imperfection.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.780 | 0.900 | 55/5 (+7 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **topology-setup — Satisfied:** node2 and node3 communicate through node1 (private links must be configured to actually route through node1)
  - **Why:** node1 eth1/eth2 and node2/node3 enp8s0 were unconfigured; executor assigned static IPs and specific routes and confirmed ttl=63 pings between node2 and node3, proving traffic transits node1 as a 3-hop path.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-fefffc5d22bf4e36`, `cmd-509e8a5317c54483`, `cmd-c7518aeb71ad4dfc`, `cmd-b56fde738ee24222`, `cmd-67e0a57acb1f4e9f`, `cmd-652b7f9d599b432c`, `cmd-5e69958f1ff14dac`, `cmd-e23b9fb70c794e13`, `cmd-e684a58ec1de4603`
- **limit-node2-to-node3 — Satisfied:** Limit traffic from node2 toward node3 to 1 Mbit/s
  - **Why:** A VyOS qos shaper policy (bandwidth/ceiling 1mbit) was applied as an egress policy on node1 eth2 (the node3-facing link). tc showed htb qdisc active, and iperf3 measured throughput dropping from a ~20 Gbps unshaped baseline to ~0.84-0.92 Mbit/s after shaping, both immediately and after all three nodes were rebooted.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-40d4ba4bd7134a41`, `cmd-f3209746bc4a495d`, `cmd-e42059756aff4edb`, `cmd-8f719c292d614cf3`, `cmd-17670c0212414c67`, `cmd-c9b5a240a6f44b24`
- **leave-node3-to-node2-unrestricted — Satisfied:** Leave traffic from node3 toward node2 unrestricted
  - **Why:** No shaper was applied to eth1 (node2-facing link). iperf3 measured ~19.1 Gbps baseline and ~1.5 Gbps post-shaping (limited only by iperf3/CPU, not by any tc policy) node3->node2, confirming the reverse direction remains unrestricted.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ddeea03a6c0e46f1`, `cmd-4f7e6ab93f1441df`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.780**. Reviewed all 67 executor commands chronologically. State-changing actions (static IP/route assignment on all three nodes, VyOS qos policy commit/save, iperf3 package installs, temporary firewalld port openings for testing) all had a clear role in establishing the topology, applying the shaper, or collecting bounded throughput evidence. Firewalld ports opened for iperf3 testing were reliably closed afterward (cmd-93acfeae24a047f9, cmd-ac126dcfa7da4b6f, cmd-6eb9dd26635647a0, cmd-6ad71c1a56f14991), and iperf3 server processes were killed after each test. However, several diagnostic/result files were left behind on node2 and node3 (/tmp/res.json, /tmp/res_shaped.json, /tmp/res_post_reboot.json, /tmp/res_final.json, /tmp/iperf_server.log, /tmp/reboot.log on node2; /tmp/res_rev.json, /tmp/res_rev_shaped.json, /tmp/iperf_server.log, /tmp/reboot.log on node3), visible in the after_executor snapshot as residue not present at before_prepare. These are low-risk, non-destructive artifacts but constitute unnecessary/uncleaned mutation. A handful of command failures (VyOS 'show'/'run' syntax not available in bash context, an initial dnf GPG-key parsing failure on node2, and python JSON KeyErrors before the iperf3 server was reachable) were read-only or self-corrected diagnostic issues with no lasting negative effect.

Hygiene evidence: `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`, `cmd-93acfeae24a047f9`, `cmd-ac126dcfa7da4b6f`, `cmd-6eb9dd26635647a0`, `cmd-6ad71c1a56f14991`

### Comments and limitations

- Restart/reboot was not part of the public task's material contract, so its evidence quality affects confidence and hygiene framing only, not the satisfied status of the three shaping/topology requirements.
- Small residual temp files (iperf3 result JSON, iperf_server.log, reboot.log) were left on node2 and node3 after testing; low-risk but not cleaned up.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.780); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
